About the role
Lumen Bank is expanding its digital lending franchise in Singapore and is hiring a Senior Product Manager to own the end-to-end journey for small-business and consumer credit products. You will report to the Head of Digital Lending and work daily with engineering, risk, compliance, design and the commercial teams.

What you will do
- Own the product roadmap for the lending application, onboarding and repayment experience, and the metrics it moves: activation, approval rate, time-to-yes and on-time repayment.
- Partner with Credit Risk and Compliance to ship changes that satisfy MAS expectations without adding friction for good customers.
- Run structured discovery with customers, relationship managers and operations teams, and turn what you learn into clear problem statements and prioritised bets.
- Design and run experiments, read the results with discipline, and decide what to scale or stop.
- Work with engineering leads on sequencing, trade-offs and delivery, keeping a squad of 10 to 15 people focused on outcomes.
- Present progress and investment cases to senior leadership every quarter.
- Coach junior product managers and help raise the quality bar across the product group.

What we are looking for
- 6+ years in product management, ideally in fintech, payments, lending or another regulated digital product.
- A track record of launching products that reached measurable adoption and revenue.
- Strong analytical skills: comfortable with SQL, funnel analysis and experiment design.
- Experience working with risk, compliance and vendors in a regulated environment.
- Excellent written and verbal communication with executives and engineers alike.
- An MBA or equivalent experience is a plus.
- Based in Singapore, with the right to work here.

Why Lumen
You will join a well-capitalised bank that is serious about digital products, with real ownership, a supportive leadership team and the chance to shape how thousands of Singapore businesses borrow.

points.overrideText: Delivered MAS-aligned onboarding and reporting changes ahead of the regulatory deadline, with zero audit findings and no drop in approval rates
